languages_frameworks: openai SDK against an OpenAI-compatible LLM endpoint (default model name glm-5.3)

implemented_capabilities.capability: Fraud-ring detection: WCC over shared-device/address/owner projection enriched with internal money-flow density
implemented_capabilities.notes: Calls FalkorDB algo.WCC over a precomputed LINKED_TO projection (built at seed time), then counts internal TRANSFER edges/amount per component to separate a ring from a household sharing a device. Seeded ring/household negative controls are synthetic.

implemented_capabilities.capability: Hub ranking and money tracing with native graph algorithms
implemented_capabilities.notes: algo.pageRank + algo.betweenness on the TRANSFER projection, algo.SPpaths for up to 3 shortest money routes, algo.maxFlow for funnel capacity. All run on FalkorDB-native procedures; the authors state they mapped the algorithm API against a FalkorDB v6 server, whereas Kairos targets 4.22 (LastLift reports algo.maxFlow non-maximal results and algo.SPpaths hangs on 4.22).

implemented_capabilities.capability: Three-tier agent memory in the graph (episodic Sessions/Messages, semantic Findings/Cases, procedural Playbooks) with learned-lesson write-back
implemented_capabilities.notes: Case -[:OPENED_IN]-> Session, Session -[:PRODUCED]-> Finding -[:ABOUT]-> Account/Device, Session -[:HANDS_OFF]-> Session, Playbook -[:STEP]-> PlaybookStep -[:LEARNED_IN]-> Case. Memory recall uses fulltext indexes and returns closed_at/learned dates. No supersession: a later contradictory Finding does not invalidate an earlier one.

implemented_capabilities.capability: Two-agent analyst -> investigator handoff with least-privilege tool menus and typed answer shapes
implemented_capabilities.notes: Real OpenAI-tool-calling loop (max 14 tool rounds) with role-restricted tool lists and a final JSON verdict (shape/verdict/confidence/summary). Behaviour rules (follow the playbook, cite policy section ids, do not act on negative controls) are LLM prompt instructions, not enforced code; the freeze/escalate writes are executed on the model's decision without a human approval step.

implemented_capabilities.capability: Per-tenant graph isolation and fixed typed tool registry exposed over MCP and REST
implemented_capabilities.notes: Each bank is its own FalkorDB graph 'bank_<slug>' validated by regex; reads always use GRAPH.RO_QUERY, writes use GRAPH.QUERY. The model never writes Cypher; unknown entities return typed ToolError shapes (unknown_entity / not_in_graph). ~27 tools registered.

Freeze/escalate create Action nodes (kind, at, by, reason) linked ACTED_ON/RECORDED_IN. PolicyDoc nodes carry version and effective date so answers can cite them. The freeze action only sets a graph property; no core-banking integration.

implemented_capabilities.capability: Deterministic seeded synthetic banks with planted ground-truth fixtures
implemented_capabilities.notes: Three synthetic tenants (~280 accounts each), two planted rings, one negative control, one past recurring case. Entirely synthetic.

graph_models_and_cypher: Data: Bank, Account, Person, Device, Address, Merchant, Transaction, Alert with OWNS, ACCESSED_FROM, LIVES_AT/REGISTERED_AT, FROM/TO, AT, ABOUT plus two algorithm projections TRANSFER(Account->Account {amount, at, channel, count}) and LINKED_TO(Account->Account {via, via_id}). Memory: Session, Message (SAID_IN, NEXT), Case (OPENED_IN, INVESTIGATES, INVOLVES, HAS_FINDING), Finding (ABOUT), Playbook/PlaybookStep (STEP, LEARNED_IN), PolicyDoc/PolicyChunk (HAS_CHUNK), Action (ACTED_ON, RECORDED_IN), HANDS_OFF between Sessions. All Cypher is hand-written with $params in _Q_* constants; reads via ro_query. FalkorDB-native procedures: algo.WCC, algo.pageRank, algo.betweenness, algo.SPpaths, algo.maxFlow, and fulltext indexes (db.idx.fulltext). No APOC/GDS. Write tools issue multiple separate GRAPH.QUERY calls per action (no single-transaction atomicity: open_case issues 3-5 writes).
algorithms: Weakly connected components over association projection with money-density enrichment in ledgerlens/tools.py:t_find_rings
PageRank + betweenness hub detection inside a component in t_rank_ring_accounts
Shortest multi-hop transfer route (algo.SPpaths, maxLen param) in t_trace_money_path
Max-flow funnel capacity (algo.maxFlow with amount capacity) in t_money_flow_capacity
Variable-length LINKED_TO|TRANSFER*..5 connection explanation in t_explain_connection
backend_interfaces: FastMCP stdio server (python -m ledgerlens.mcp_server) exposing the same tool registry with a required tenant argument
frontend_interfaces: static/console.html (single-file investigator console) and docs/index.html (static docs page)
agent_or_memory_mechanisms: Two OpenAI-compatible tool-calling agents (intake analyst, case investigator) coordinating through the graph: the handoff is a HANDS_OFF edge between Session nodes. Episodic, semantic and procedural memory are explicit graph structures; the investigator can append a learned PlaybookStep sourced to the case that taught it, so procedure evolves across sessions (tests/test_evolution.py). Fixed tool menu with per-role least privilege.
tests_present: tests/ has 7 files with ~35 test functions: test_rings.py (8), test_evolution.py (6), test_memory.py (6), test_shapes.py (6), test_isolation.py (4), test_agent_llm.py (3, needs a live LLM, marker 'llm'), test_concurrency.py (2); they assert tools recover exactly the planted rings from tests/fixtures/planted_*.json and need a live FalkorDB. Not executed by auditor.
security_findings: ledgerlens/service.py:101-213 - no authentication or authorization on any route, including POST /api/tenants/{t}/investigate and /api/bench, which let any caller trigger LLM calls and graph writes; tenant isolation depends only on a URL path slug validated by regex.

ledgerlens/tools.py:572-588 (t_freeze_account) and :590-601 (t_escalate_case) - model-initiated state-changing actions with no human-approval gate; the only guard is prompt text in agents.py (INVESTIGATOR_SYSTEM).

ledgerlens/tools.py:526-679 - each write tool performs several independent GRAPH.QUERY calls (no transaction), so a mid-way failure leaves partial case/finding/session structure; t_record_message chain-linking uses a non-atomic 'no NEXT yet' heuristic that can mis-link under concurrency (tests/test_concurrency.py covers 2 cases).
ledgerlens/tools.py:313-334 and 286-310 - algo.maxFlow / algo.SPpaths calls are on the request path without a pure-Python fallback; see LastLift notes on FalkorDB 4.22 defects/hangs.
docker-compose.yml - falkordb/falkordb:latest (unpinned) with no password; port not published (internal network only), app container binds 0.0.0.0:8000 behind an external reverse-proxy network.
ledgerlens/config.py:15-17 - LLM_API_KEY read from env; no hard-coded secrets found. No eval/exec/subprocess/pickle in ledgerlens/, seed.py, app.py or scripts/.

ledgerlens/service.py:ask - free-text user message is passed to the LLM tool loop (prompt-injection surface): findings from LLM summaries are persisted verbatim to Finding.text and later recalled as memory (stored-prompt-injection / memory-poisoning path).
duplicates_or_overlaps: Financial Fraud ring detection overlaps ManjariYagnik/GraphHacks (RingLens) and other fraud-ring entries; the explicit three-type agent memory plus handoff edges overlaps the 'Agent Memory & Provenance' family. Algorithms (WCC/pageRank/betweenness/maxFlow/SPpaths) are FalkorDB built-ins, so little unique algorithm code.
evidence_drift_relevance: MEDIUM - findings carry at/confidence/source and link to entities, learned playbook steps carry LEARNED_IN provenance, policy docs carry version and effective date, and memory answers must state when they were learned; but there is no supersession, expiry or dependency invalidation, and actions are not re-checked against changed evidence.

strongest_reusable_unit.why: A compact, tested pattern for graph-resident agent memory (case/finding/session/playbook with HANDS_OFF handoffs and learned-lesson provenance), tenant-per-graph isolation and a typed fixed tool registry exposed identically over REST and MCP. The ring-detection tools are thin wrappers over FalkorDB algorithms and need the projection-building seed logic to be useful.
strongest_reusable_unit.external_runtime_needed: FalkorDB with algo.* procedures (verify on 4.22); OpenAI-compatible LLM endpoint only for the agents

strategy_rationale: Natural Financial Fraud domain pack for Kairos (ring detection tools, projections, negative-control tests) plus a reference design for graph-native episodic/semantic/procedural agent memory; algorithm calls must be validated or replaced on FalkorDB 4.22 and the action tools need an approval gate before reuse.
